record.paper_title: Some open problems in the context of skew PBW extensions and semi-graded rings
record.original_question: For an Artin-Schelter regular algebra A, must A always be a domain?

evidence.quote: (iii) Artin-Schelter open problems: In [9] were formulated the following problems: 2. Any AS algebra is a domain?

There are some advances with respect to the previous open problems: Both questions above have positive answer for any AS algebra of dimension ≤ 3. In addition, the same is true for all known concrete examples of AS algebras of higher dimension. If A is AS noetherian and its dimension is ≤ 4, then A is a domain.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0} A_n$ be a connected graded $k$-algebra (so $A_0=k$ and $A$ is finitely generated in degree $\geq 1$). Recall that $A$ is called Artin–Schelter regular if:

(1) $A$ has finite global dimension $d<\infty$;
(2) $A$ has finite Gelfand–Kirillov dimension; and
(3) $A$ is Artin–Schelter Gorenstein, meaning that
$$\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{A}(k,A)=\begin{cases} 0 & i\neq d,\\ k(\ell) & i=d,\end{cases}$$
for some integer $\ell$ (the AS index), where $k=A/A_{\geq 1}$ is the trivial module.

Question: Must every Artin–Schelter regular algebra $A$ (in the sense above) be a domain, i.e., have no nonzero zero-divisors?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question is widely regarded as open. Positive answers are known in restricted cases: every AS-regular algebra of global dimension at most 3 is a domain; every noetherian AS-regular algebra of dimension at most 4 is a domain; and every noetherian PI Artin–Schelter regular algebra is a domain (and a maximal order in its quotient division ring). All known concrete higher-dimensional examples are domains, but no proof is known in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Artin–Schelter regular algebras discussing the classification and properties; the domain property is established in low dimension and for PI cases.
status_evidence.claim: Domain property is known in low dimensions and for PI AS-regular algebras, while remaining open in general.

status_evidence.title: Artin-Schelter regular algebra (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Artin–Schelter regular algebras are noncommutative analogues of polynomial rings; many known examples are domains.
status_evidence.claim: All known examples of AS-regular algebras are domains.
